title: Trace the order of try, catch and finally

blocks.text: The `finally` block runs after the `try` and `catch` blocks whether an exception was thrown or not, and even when the `try` block exits with `return`.
Write `Flow.run(IntSupplier body, List<String> log)`. It records what runs, in order, in `log`:

items: `"try"` as the `try` block starts, then it evaluates `body` and returns its value;
when `body` throws an `IllegalStateException`, `"catch " + message`, and `run` returns `-1`;

blocks.text: Any other exception from `body` is not caught: it leaves `run`.
Page Q2's own example is a `try` that returns while a `finally` still prints. Check every way out of your method.

cases.says: A handled failure runs the try, then the catch, then the finally.
A return in the try block does not skip the finally block: it runs before the method returns.
An exception no catch handles still runs the finally block on its way out.

concepts: A return in the try block does not skip finally: it runs before the method returns.
The finally block runs after the try and catch blocks whether or not an exception was thrown or caught.
